seen.cipher: Calendar: 'John Poingdexter to [blank]. Dublin. 2 Jan. ... The King's army [a passage follows in cipher]. This place is blockaded by the Parliament ships'. The entry sits after the 26 and 30 Dec 1645 items of vol. CCLXI, so the year is 1645/6; no decipherment is mentioned and the calendar omits the passage.

prior_art.decode: known.py 'Poingdexter', 'SP 63/261', 'Glamorgan': no DECODE record or ledger hit for this letter (only unrelated Glamorgan-treaty catalogue entries).
prior_art.tomokiyo: Web searches for Poingdexter/Dublin January 1646 cipher and the Irish 1640s ciphers returned no cryptiana page on this letter; Tomokiyo's unsolved list (mirrored in the repo) has no entry for it.
prior_art.lasry: No Lasry/DECODE decipherment of a Dublin 1646 letter is known to the repo (known.py) or found by web search (searches of 29 Oct 2026).
prior_art.edition: The Mahaffy calendar itself is the edition and omits the cipher; the neighbouring entries were read for a decipherment note: none. Sender name looks garbled ('Poingdexter', possibly Poyntz) and the recipient is blank in print.
prior_art.literature: Web search on the sender, the passage wording and 'State Papers Ireland cipher 1646' found only unrelated Dublin 1646 letters (Crouther to Lenthall, Du to Le Tellier).

vetting.key_check: No key for a Dublin 1645-46 correspondent is held in the repo or on DECODE; the Ormond-Digby ciphers of the same years (targets/rupert, Add MS 18983) were not tried because no image of the leaf exists.
vetting.duplicates: known.py 'Poingdexter', 'SP 63/261', 'Glamorgan': no catalogue entry or lead is this letter; other Glamorgan-period hits are separate letters.

prior_art.decode: A-10 is not among the Salazar volumes on DECODE (9/8, 9/17, 9/23-9/31, 9/34 only); known.py 'A-10', 'Francisco de Rojas', 'Santo Domingo' found no record for this letter.

prior_art.edition: The catalogue entry carries only an Observaciones note on the first three bishops, no 'Publicada por'; Rodriguez Villa's 1896 study of Rojas (BRAH) was found in search but not checked for this letter, so a printed copy is not excluded.
prior_art.literature: Web searches for Rojas as ambassador (Pascual Molina and Fiz Fuertes 2015; Fernandez de Cordoba Miralles 2014) surfaced studies of the man, none of this cipher letter.

vetting.key_check: Cifra general of the Catholic Monarchs (BRAH 9/15, DECODE R9815-R9832) is the likely system for a royal letter to Rome in 1504 but cannot be applied without an image of the leaf; no key for the Ferdinand-Rojas correspondence is held here.
vetting.duplicates: known.py 'A-10', 'Francisco de Rojas', 'Santo Domingo': only sibling Salazar A-10 entries (inv. 952, 958) of earlier batches, which are other letters.

seen.cipher: Calendar no. 301: 'Translation of a letter from the minister of Hanover to Prince Ferdinand. It relates to a letter from the Duc de Broglio, of the 17th past, which his Serene Highness had sent to London to be deciphered, but the contents of which they had not then succeeded in wholly making out. (French.) 1 p.' The ciphered Broglie letter is not the calendared document.

prior_art.decode: known.py 'Broglie', 'Prince Ferdinand', 'Regencies': no DECODE record or ledger entry for this item (only a Broglie sentence in a README and a Calames list).
prior_art.tomokiyo: Web search (Broglie 1760 lettre chiffree interceptee, Ferdinand) found no cryptiana page; none known.
prior_art.lasry: No Lasry/DECODE item for Broglie 1760 found by known.py or by the web searches of 29 Oct 2026.
prior_art.edition: Redington's calendar is the only print; it gives the translation's gist and does not print the cipher. A web search of TNA Discovery found intercepted Broglie letters of Aug 1760 in SP 87/38 (e.g. SP 87/38/48, /50, /52), none described as cipher.
prior_art.literature: Web searches for the 17 Aug 1760 Broglie letter and its decipherment found nothing beyond those SP 87/38 catalogue lines.

vetting.key_check: No French army key of 1760 is held in the repo or DECODE; nothing to apply because there is no cipher leaf in the calendared item.
vetting.duplicates: known.py 'Broglie' 'Prince Ferdinand' 'Regencies': no catalogue entry; the SP 87/38 intercepts could be a separate lead.
vetting.closed: The calendared document (Home Office no. 301) is a clear French translation about a Broglie letter sent to London for deciphering; the ciphered Broglie letter is not identified. The SP 87/38 intercepted Broglie letters of Aug 1760 would need their own lead.
